lore.title: The dead
lore.text: The dead are slow, but they never tire and they follow noise. A bite brings a fever within a day, and those who die of it get up again. Nobody here knows of a cure. Television went dark in the second week, and the phones soon after.

lore.title: The highway strip
lore.text: The strip was the busy end of town: trucks stopped for diesel and pie at the diner, farmers bought seed and fencing at the feed store. The gas station's pumps went dry on day six, and its little shop was cleaned out before that.

lore.title: Main Street
lore.text: Main Street is two blocks of brick storefronts around the courthouse. The pharmacy was looted early but its back room has a steel door. The church bell rang every hour for the first week, until someone made it stop; the dead still drift toward the square out of habit.

lore.title: The houses
lore.text: Behind Main Street are a few hundred small houses and a trailer park by the creek. Most doors stand open. Pantries, garages and medicine cabinets are worth searching, but the dead linger indoors where they turned, and a quiet house is not always an empty one.

lore.title: The highway junction
lore.text: A few miles out, the two-lane meets the interstate under a concrete overpass. Abandoned cars fill both lanes for a mile in each direction, many with their doors open and luggage still in the trunks. Anyone travelling by road has to pass through or around it.

lore.title: Ridge
lore.text: Ridge is the next town up the ridge road, smaller and poorer than this one. Its people walled off the school and the grain elevator with trucks and fencing in the first days. Traders who went up there early came back with flour; lately, nobody has gone.

lore.title: The evacuation
lore.text: On day four the county organised an evacuation from the clinic on Main Street. Buses were to take people to the interstate and on to a camp. The clinic was overrun before half had boarded, the buses that got away never came back, and nobody has heard from the camp.

lore.title: Harmon's Hardware
lore.text: Harmon's is a single-storey cinderblock store with a steel roll-down front, which is why it held. The shelves still carry tools, rope, tarps, fasteners and garden supplies. The power is off; a battery lantern and the skylights light the sales floor.

lore.title: The roof
lore.text: A ladder in the manager's office climbs to a roof hatch. From the flat tar roof you can see the whole highway strip, the water tower and the first houses of town. It is the best lookout for miles, and the worst place to be caught in the open.

lore.title: Gil Ferris
lore.text: Gil Ferris bought the store from old Walt Harmon thirty years ago and never changed the sign. He knows every shelf and half the town by name, coached Little League for a decade, and still counts the till drawer every night out of habit.

timeline.text: The first cases reached the county hospital; within two days the town was under a stay-at-home order.
The county evacuation from the Main Street clinic broke down in panic before half the people had boarded the buses.
The gas station's pumps on the highway strip ran dry.
Ridge closes the ridge road: its people block it with trucks and turn back anyone who comes without something to trade.

scenario.opening:
Morning light comes through the gaps in the plywood in thin gold stripes. Marlene is already up, counting cans in the stockroom for the third time this week and writing the number on the wall in marker. Four days, the number says.

Dex paces the sales floor with the shotgun, checking the windows that don't need checking. Ruth sits cross-legged on the floor beside a disassembled generator, sleeves pushed up, not talking to anyone. Gil Ferris, who owns this place and won't let anyone forget it, has the office door shut again.

"Herd's still coming," Dex says to no one in particular. "Saw it from the roof at dawn. Maybe a day out."

Marlene looks up from her cans and meets your eyes, like she's waiting to hear what you think.

characterData.name: Jordan Pike
characterData.want: keep this group alive long enough to find somewhere safer
characterData.voice: Few words, dry humor, calm under pressure.
characterData.description: Drove the same county routes for ten years and knows every back road. Ended up at Harmon's by chance and stayed because someone had to keep things steady.
characterData.appearance: Medium build in a faded courier jacket, with short dark hair, a road-map tattoo on one forearm and a crowbar never far from reach.
knows: Gil Ferris keeps the office locked even at night and gets defensive when anyone goes near it.

characterData.name: Marlene Ortiz
characterData.want: keep everyone fed and together, and never abandon anyone again
characterData.secret: On day nine she left her previous group behind during an overrun to save herself. She tells people she was the only survivor.
characterData.voice: Calm and warm, calls people 'honey', goes cold when angry.
characterData.description: Thirty years in an emergency room left her calm in a crisis and impossible to fool about a wound. She keeps the food count and everyone's spirits.
characterData.appearance: Short and solid, with silver hair pinned up, reading glasses on a cord and a nurse's watch she still checks out of habit.

characterData.name: Dex Coleman
characterData.want: get to his sister's last known location in the next county
characterData.secret: Two days ago something scratched his forearm during a supply run. He wrapped it and tells himself it was broken glass.
characterData.voice: Loud, quick, military slang, jokes when scared.
characterData.description: Army reserve, two weekends a month, until the world ended. Brave, loud and loyal; the one who stands watch without being asked.

This story is: survival, horror, grim. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.

- horror: Dread builds slowly; imply more than you show; quiet moments feel uneasy.
- grim: Hard choices without good options; kindness costs something, and losses stay lost.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
